question: Can a STATISTICAL criterion for which slots to overwrite (redundancy / QA Fisher / their combination) beat the incumbent attention-mass ranker -- specifically, run in REVERSE: spend the 0.57 of QA slack to buy MT bandwidth by gating on redundancy at larger top_t?
variable_under_test: SLOT_SELECTION in {tfidf, redundancy, fisher, mass_x_redundancy} x TOP_T in {32,64,128}; everything else held at the project's current best point (KEY_MODE=highest_attention, AM_KEY_REPOSITION=1, AM_ROPE_THETA=5000000, ENABLE_BETA=0, GRANULARITY=per_layer, USE_IDF=0, RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4, RIDGE_SCALE=spectral, DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2, MAX_QUERIES_PER_HEAD=64)
baseline_ref: C0_control in this bundle == MECH-005/DIAG-KEYCURVE (QA 1.9560 / MT 2.2720 at k=12)

numbers._note: qa/mt are the BEST new selector's own optima -- mass_x_redundancy at TOP_T=32 (QA 1.89434 at k=8, MT 2.37893 at k=16). NO ARM BEAT THE CONTROL ON MT: every arm's best MT is 0.107-0.397 WORSE than the control's 2.27202, all clearing DIAG-NOISE's +-0.049 paired resolution. The only resolved WIN anywhere is fisher's retention: QA 1.86411 (k=12), -0.0823 vs the control's own best QA 1.94640 -- bought at +0.3972 MT. Fisher-scoring cost 98.8 s of DIAGNOSTIC backward, paid once offline and cached (state/diagnostics/slot_fisher_qa_phase1.npz); it is not an optimizer step and every arm here ran gradient_steps = 0.

bandwidth_vs_acquisition._definition: Across the 6 arms, does the SELECTION's measured write bandwidth predict acquisition, and its retention exposure predict forgetting? Both are the causal link DIAG-IMPORTANCE's Pareto table asserts.

measured_vs_projected_bandwidth._definition: DIAG-IMPORTANCE projected a redundancy gate at TOP_T=64 -> ~34.6% MT routing mass and TOP_T=128 -> ~69%. Measured, from the runs' own saved per-document masks:
measured_vs_projected_bandwidth.verdict: The projection was a linear extrapolation of a DIFFERENT selector (best-32-within-the-most-redundant-quartile, which is mass-ranked INSIDE a redundancy constraint). Pure top-t-by-redundancy is 2.4-3.2x below it: even at 4x the budget (TOP_T=128) it captures LESS MT routing mass (0.2146) than the incumbent does at TOP_T=32 (0.2799). The reverse trade cannot reach parity, let alone exceed it.

fisher_cost.source: DIAG-IMPORTANCE::collect_fisher on the same untouched Phase-1 cartridge
fisher_cost.leakage_caveat: scored on the QA EVAL split (matching DIAG-IMPORTANCE), so F32's QA number is an optimistic bound on retention; its MT number is unaffected and is what the arm was dispatched to test.

command: FILES EDITED (MECH-008, all opt-in / default off): cartridges/am/ranking.py (+SLOT_PRIOR_SELECTIONS, compute_slot_redundancy, load_slot_fisher_scores, _unit_rank, _mask_from_topk, _rank_slot_prior_per_layer, _check_prior_shape; rank_am_slots gains a cache=None keyword), cartridges/am/finetune.py (slot_selection Literal += 3 modes; new fields redundancy_ridge_rel=1e-6 / mass_redundancy_alpha=0.5 / slot_fisher_path=None; passes cache= at the decoupled call site), cartridges/am/continual.py (passes cache=), cartridges/am/__init__.py (exports), examples/qasper2/train/continual_am_sparse.py (AM_SLOT_FISHER_PATH / AM_REDUNDANCY_RIDGE_REL / AM_MASS_REDUNDANCY_ALPHA + _slot_prior_kwargs() conditional-kwarg guard). 476 insertions, 2 deletions across 5 files. RUN: bash research_loop/results/MECH-INFOGATE/launch_mech_infogate.sh (flock one GPU, PYTHONPATH pinned to _explore, 6 AM Phase-2 runs + 48 dual-split evals at k in {8,10,12,16}). SANITY: research_loop/results/MECH-INFOGATE/sanity_mech008.py (CPU).
observations: MECH-008 built (three opt-in SLOT_SELECTION modes: redundancy, fisher, mass_x_redundancy) and tested on six AM Phase-2 arms, every arm evaluated on BOTH splits at k = 8, 10, 12, 16 (48 evals). DEFAULT PRESERVED: the tfidf control reproduced QA 1.9560121297836304 / MT 2.2720184326171875 at k=12 and QA 2.034916400909424 / MT 2.330503463745117 at k=16 to all 16 digits (GATE_PASS), so the mechanism is numerically inert when off. UNIT LEVEL: compute_slot_redundancy reproduces DIAG-IMPORTANCE's score_redundancy array EXACTLY (max|diff| = 0.0 at ridge_rel 1e-6, 1e-4 and 1e-8; Spearman 1.0; per-layer top-32 set agreement 1.0000) and the selectors reproduce its measured top-32 overlaps with the incumbent (redundancy 0.1068 vs 0.107 published, lowest-Fisher 0.0009 vs 0.0009); mass_x_redundancy degenerates exactly to attention_mass at alpha=0 and to redundancy at alpha=1. THE REVERSE TRADE DOES NOT WORK. Best MT per arm (own-optimum k): control 2.27202 (k=12), redundancy t32 2.43865, t64 2.48107, t128 2.45815, mass_x_redundancy t32 2.37893, fisher t32 2.66917 -- all six new points are 0.107 to 0.397 WORSE on MT than the control, and every one of those deltas clears DIAG-NOISE's paired MT resolution of 0.049 (by 2.2x to 8.1x). Raising top_t under the redundancy gate did not buy acquisition: t=64 and t=128 are WORSE on MT than t=32 and monotonically worse on QA (best QA 1.9247 -> 1.9389 -> 2.0611). THE MEASURED CAUSE. From the runs' own saved per-document masks, the realised share of writable MT routing mass is control 0.2799, redundancy 0.0662 / 0.1195 / 0.2146 at t=32/64/128, mass_x_redundancy 0.1251, fisher 0.0104 -- i.e. the redundancy gate at FOUR TIMES the budget still captures LESS MT bandwidth (0.2146) than the incumbent does at t=32 (0.2799). DIAG-IMPORTANCE's projection (~34.6% at t=64, ~69% at t=128) was a linear extrapolation of a different selector -- best-32-WITHIN-the-most-redundant-quartile, which is mass-ranked inside a redundancy constraint -- and pure top-t-by-redundancy sits 2.4-3.2x below it. Across the six arms log(realised MT routing mass) predicts best MT loss at Pearson -0.877 (Spearman -0.714) and realised QA Fisher exposure predicts best QA loss at Spearman +0.771, so both halves of the Pareto trade are confirmed at the LOSS level, not just at the mass level. THE ONE RESOLVED WIN IS ON THE WRONG AXIS: fisher t32 gives the best retention measured in this bundle, QA 1.86411 at k=12 (-0.0823 vs the control's own best QA 1.94640, 1.5x the paired QA resolution), while exposing 0.0004 of QA Fisher mass and 0.0104 of MT mass -- and it costs +0.3972 MT. That is the anti-alignment prediction confirmed end to end. mass_x_redundancy is the least-bad new selector on both axes (QA 1.89434 at k=8, -0.0521 vs control, just INSIDE the QA resolution; MT 2.37893, +0.1069, outside). NO ARM MEETS THE TARGET (QA <= 2.52 AND MT <= 2.02); every arm clears the QA budget by 0.39-0.66 and misses the MT budget by 0.36-0.65. COST IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR: solve time is 312-358 s across all six arms (0.89x-1.02x the control), so a 4x larger top_t is essentially free here; am/mean_mse 0.0032-0.0047 and |v|max 74.5-91.5 are all in the control's range, so nothing failed numerically. gradient_steps = 0 in every arm; the Fisher scoring pass (98.8 s of diagnostic backward, 78 QA + 69 MT examples) was paid once offline and cached. CAVEATS: (a) the Fisher array is scored on the QA EVAL split, matching DIAG-IMPORTANCE, so F32's QA number is an optimistic bound -- its MT number, which is what the arm was dispatched to test, is unaffected; (b) every arm is a single seed (AM_SEED_OFFSET unset), so the deltas are compared against the paired resolution, not against a seed-varied interval; (c) three of the five new arms have their MT minimum at k=16, the edge of the evaluated set, so their true minima are unlocated and the comparison is if anything generous to them; (d) redundancy is recomputed from the LIVE cache at every document, so it drifts as slots are written -- at document 0 it is exactly DIAG-IMPORTANCE's array.
interpretation_requested_by_the_brief_no: The brief's decision rule reads: 'MT flat or worse at every top_t => the anti-alignment is binding, and the gating family is closed with a measured cause.' MT is worse than the incumbent at every top_t and for every information-theoretic criterion tried, by margins 2.2x-8.1x the measured paired resolution, and the cause is measured rather than inferred: the realised write bandwidth of a redundancy-gated selection at TOP_T=128 (0.2146 of writable MT routing mass) is still below the incumbent's at TOP_T=32 (0.2799), and bandwidth predicts acquisition across arms at Pearson -0.877. The reverse trade therefore cannot be run by raising top_t under these gates: redundancy is 'at chance' with respect to MT-wanted, and a chance-level selector at 4x the budget still loses to a targeted selector at 1x, because the incumbent's bandwidth is concentrated, not diffuse.
